mutations.because: K-D9's only refusal is a duplicate t on one track's same clock. Disabling the check lets two stops at the exact same t on the same clock through, which K-D9 refuses. (Re-anchored by ANCHORS: K1b made a track single-clock, so the per-clock map became one `seenT` set and the duplicate-`t` refusal this mutation disables reads from it directly; The semantic edit is the same one; the after-text is that edit re-expressed against the current shape, not a new claim.)

K-D8 scopes the duplicate-t refusal PER CLOCK: two stops sharing a t on different clocks are independent axes and legal. Collapsing the per-clock seen-set to one set across all clocks makes a legal cross-clock duplicate look refused.
mutations.retired: Retired by ANCHORS: a later decision reversed the claim. K1b made a track SINGLE-clock — two clocks on one property are now two tracks — so the per-clock `seenTByClock` map this mutation collapses is exactly the `seenT` set the module ships today. The mutant is the current code, and a cross-clock duplicate inside one track is no longer legal for this mutation to defend. The surviving half of K-D9, that a duplicate `t` is refused at all, is still pinned by k1a.json#0.

mutations.because: orderedKeys appends unnamed keys at the end, so dropping tracks from LAYER_KEY_ORDER does not make it disappear — it falls into the same tail bucket as any other unrecognised key, which a plain 'tracks appears in the output' assertion cannot tell apart from tracks sitting at its declared position. Only a fixture with an unnamed key written before tracks in source order proves the position. (Re-anchored by ANCHORS: AR1 inserted `link` into LAYER_KEY_ORDER, which Prettier reformatted onto separate lines; the semantic edit — `tracks` dropped from the order — is the same one.)
